metadata.case_name: PUK CHUNG YU v. LAM SHUI KEUNG AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: Second degree burn over right neck and back regions
source: the plaintiff was immediately sent to the A&E of CMC where he was found to have second degree burn over his right neck and back regions.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the neck

injuries.description: Operation for debridement and skin grafting with graft taken from right lateral thigh
injuries.body_part: right lateral thigh (donor site); operated sites
source: the plaintiff was transferred to the Department of Surgery at PWH for an operation for debridement and skin grafting on 10 January 2007 with a graft taken from the plaintiff’s right lateral thigh.
injuries.icd_description: Open wound of hip or thigh, unspecified

injuries.description: Skin graft donor area scar on right lateral thigh
source:
Right lateral thigh: A skin graft donor area scar was readily
noticeable, measuring 14 cm x 4 cm. The scar was pale, flat but with a
thickened coarse texture. There is a noticeable raised thickened posterior
margin along 1 cm of the scar. Although the scar can be concealed by clothing,
it will be evident when the plaintiff wears swimsuit or above-knee shorts. The
scar cannot be surgically improved.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of hip or thigh

injuries.description: Scar at right upper posterior aspect of neck
source:
Upper neck: A scar was readily noticeable at the right upper posterior
aspect, measuring 4 cm x 2 cm. The lower 0.5 cm of the margin was raised and
thickened. This will always be noticeable and can only be partially concealed
by clothing.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of neck

injuries.description: Scar at right lower neck adjacent to shoulder region
injuries.body_part: right lower neck adjacent to shoulder region
source:
Lower neck: Another scar was readily noticeable at right lower part
adjacent to shoulder region, measuring 6.5 cm x 3.5 cm. The scar is soft and
pliable with a slight coarse texture. This will always be noticeable and can
only be partially concealed by clothing.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of neck

injuries.description: Occipital scalp scar with bald patch and raised hairline
source:
Occipital area: A noticeable bald patch scar can be seen at the lower
occipital scalp, measuring 1.4 cm x 1 cm. The scar is partially concealed by
hair. There was also a raised hairline at the occipital hair margin of about 2
cm. These can be surgically restored by a more complex procedure when the
plaintiff grows older.

injuries.description: Small stitch sinus with retained debris and possible stitch remnant on margin of scar area
source:
There was also a small stitch sinus measuring 1 cm x 0.5 cm with
retained debris and possible stitch remnant on the margin of the scar area,
but this can be surgically removed.

manifestations.description: Permanent cosmetic injuries (scars) as a result of burn injury
Discomfort associated with wearing pressure garment

treatments_received.treatment: A&E attendance at Caritas Medical Centre
source: the plaintiff was immediately sent to the A&E of CMC where he was found to have second degree burn over his right neck and back regions.

treatments_received.treatment: Debridement and skin grafting (operation) on 10 January 2007
source: the plaintiff was transferred to the Department of Surgery at PWH for an operation for debridement and skin grafting on 10 January 2007 with a graft taken from the plaintiff’s right lateral thigh.

treatments_received.treatment: Occupational therapy for scar management (silicone gel, pressure therapy, massage of aqueous cream)
source: Various treatments including application of silicone gel, pressure therapy and massage of aqueous cream were prescribed to manage those scars.

the plaintiff was referred by Ha Kwai Chung Child Assessment Centre to them for motor training. The diagnosis of his condition was “borderline delay”. The plaintiff started receiving physiotherapy from 22 January 2009.
the cost of removing the stitch sinus (HK$6,000.00)
treatments_future.vmis_procedure: Local excision or destruction of lesion or tissue of skin and subcutaneous tissue

treatments_future.treatment: Removal of bald patch at occipital scalp
source: the cost for removing the bald patch at the plaintiff’s occipital scalp (HK$16,000.00)
treatments_future.vmis_procedure: Local excision or destruction of lesion or tissue of skin and subcutaneous tissue

treatments_future.treatment: More complex procedure to surgically restore occipital hairline when older
source: These can be surgically restored by a more complex procedure when the plaintiff grows older.

losses.description: Permanent cosmetic injuries and scars at right lateral thigh (donor area), right upper neck, right lower neck adjacent to shoulder region, occipital scalp (bald patch and raised hairline) and a stitch sinus; scars will be noticeable and only partially concealable by clothing.
